cases.sentence: Я знаю, ты можешь все, и невозможно противиться ___.
cases.translation: I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.
cases.explain: The verb противиться (resist/oppose) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Ты спросил, кто этот невежда, омрачающий мой замысел с ___.
cases.translation: You asked, 'Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?'
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Я говорил о тех чудесных ___, которых я не знал.
cases.translation: I have uttered that which I didn't understand, things too wonderful for me, which I didn't know.
cases.explain: The preposition о (about) governs the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Ты сказал, «Внимай ___, и я буду говорить.»
cases.translation: You said, 'Listen, now, and I will speak.'
cases.explain: The verb внимай (listen) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Я только слышал о тебе, а теперь мои глаза видят ___.
cases.translation: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
cases.explain: The transitive verb видят (see) requires the accusative case for its direct object.

cases.sentence: Поэтому я отступаю и раскаиваюсь в ___ и пепле.
cases.translation: Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) governs the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Мой ___ Иов помолится о вас, и я приму его молитву.
cases.translation: My servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept him.
cases.explain: Слуга is the subject of the verb помолится (will pray), taking the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Каждый из них дал ему по ___ и по золотому кольцу.
cases.translation: Everyone also gave him a piece of money, and everyone a ring of gold.
cases.explain: The preposition по (each) when used distributively governs the dative case.

reading.ru: Я знаю, ты можешь все, и невозможно противиться тебе.
reading.question: What does Job acknowledge about God's power?
options: God can do all things and cannot be resisted
reading.correct: God can do all things and cannot be resisted
reading.explain: Job says directly: 'I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.'

reading.ru: Я только слышал о тебе, а теперь мои глаза видят тебя, поэтому я отступаю и раскаиваюсь в прахе и пепле.
reading.question: How does Job's understanding of God change in this passage?
options: He moves from hearing about God to directly witnessing Him
reading.correct: He moves from hearing about God to directly witnessing Him
reading.explain: Job contrasts 'I had heard of you' with 'now my eye sees you', showing his deepened spiritual experience.

reading.ru: Я разгневан на тебя и на двух твоих друзей за то, что вы говорили обо мне не так верно, как мой слуга Иов.
reading.question: Why is God angry with Eliphaz and his friends?
options: Because they did not speak rightly about God as Job did
Because they refused to help Job
reading.correct: Because they did not speak rightly about God as Job did
reading.explain: God explicitly states they have not spoken rightly about Him as Job has.

reading.ru: Все его братья и сестры и все, кто знал его прежде, пришли и ели с ним у него в доме.
reading.question: What did Job's family and acquaintances do when they came to him?
options: They ate with him in his house
reading.correct: They ate with him in his house
reading.explain: The text says they 'ate with him' (ели с ним) 'in his house' (у него в доме).

reading.ru: У него теперь было тринадцать тысяч овец, шесть тысяч верблюдов, тысяча пар волов и тысяча ослиц.
reading.question: How much livestock did God restore to Job?
options: Thirteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys
Only a few sheep and goats
Half of what he had before
reading.correct: Thirteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys
reading.explain: The passage lists these specific numbers of livestock that God gave to Job.

reading.ru: После этого Иов прожил еще 140 лет. Он видел своих детей и детей своих детей до четвертого поколения.
reading.question: How long did Job live after his restoration, and how many generations did he see?
options: 140 years, and he saw his descendants to the fourth generation
40 years, and he saw only his children
70 years, and he saw only his grandchildren
100 years, and he saw his great-grandchildren only
reading.correct: 140 years, and he saw his descendants to the fourth generation
reading.explain: The text explicitly states Job lived 140 more years and saw his descendants to four generations.
